name: md5sum
one_line: compute and check MD5 message digests
plain: `md5sum` turns a file (or text) into a 32-character fingerprint. The same input always gives the same fingerprint; change one byte and the fingerprint changes completely.

Use it to check that a download was not corrupted, or that two files are identical. MD5 is broken for security (an attacker can build two different files with one MD5), so do not use it to trust a file. In CTFs it is often the format of a hash you must crack.
when: Verify a downloaded file against a published checksum.
Make an MD5 of a string to test a hash cracker.
Check a list of files from a checksum file.

examples.title: Hash a file
examples.explain: Prints the fingerprint and the file name.

examples.title: Hash a piece of text
examples.explain: echo -n leaves out the newline. Without -n the result is different, which is a very common mistake when you test a hash.

examples.title: Write a checksum list and verify it
examples.explain: The first line records the hashes. -c reads the list and prints OK or FAILED for each file.

examples.title: Only show failures
examples.explain: --quiet hides the OK lines so you see only problems.

examples.title: Are two files identical?
examples.explain: Same fingerprint, same content (for practical purposes).

examples.title: Find duplicate files
examples.explain: Hashes every file, sorts, and prints lines whose first 32 characters repeat: duplicates.

options.plain: Read in binary mode (the default on Linux).
Read sums from a file and check them.
Print in BSD style: MD5 (file) = hash.
End output lines with NUL, not newline.
With -c, do not print OK lines.
With -c, print nothing; use the exit status.
With -c, fail on badly formatted lines.

mistakes: Forgetting echo -n: the newline changes the hash.
Comparing the hash by eye: use md5sum -c or diff.
Running md5sum on a directory: it only handles files.
try: Hash 'password' with and without echo -n and compare.
Crack that MD5 with john or hashcat.
Modify one character in a file and watch the hash change completely.
see_also: sha256sum(1), sha1sum(1), cksum(1), openssl(1) (openssl dgst), john(8), hashcat(1).
captured_with: Examples are written to explain a technique; they are not captured output.
